4. 2.7. Refined decay estimates. Once the solution $U^{\mathrm{per}}$ of Proposition 4.5 is known to exist, we can bootstrap it to satisfy $O(e^{2 \tau a})$ decay in all $H^{k}, k\geq0$ , as claimed in Theorem 1.3. First, the estimate (4.43) on G is already satisfied for all N Second, the estimates on $B(U^{\mathrm{per}}, U^{\mathrm{per}})$ and $LU^{\mathrm{per}}$ above gain 1/2 derivative above the regularity of the solution. By Duhamel's formula, we see that if $N>5/2$ (not necessarily integral) and

$$
\sup _ {\tau \in (- \infty , T ]} e ^ {- (a + \varepsilon_ {0}) \tau} \| U ^ {\mathrm {p e r}} (\cdot , \tau) \| _ {H ^ {N}} < + \infty ,
$$

(4.49)

then

$$
\sup _ {\tau \in (- \infty , T ]} e ^ {- 2 a \tau} \| U ^ {\mathrm {p e r}} (\cdot , \tau) \| _ {H ^ {N + 1 / 2}} < + \infty .
$$

(4.50)

By induction, we conclude that (4.50) holds for all $N > 5/2.$

Remark 4.8 (General backgrounds). It is possible to treat more general unstable backgrounds satisfying the natural decay conditions

$$
\left| \nabla^ {k} \bar {U} (\xi) \right| \lesssim_ {k} \langle \xi \rangle^ {- k - 1}
$$
